### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.test

### Description

I have a simple test I want to write, the function is a wrapper for vim.system running rg.

```lua
T["search_async"] = new_set()

T["search_async"]["should find files with search term in content"] = function()
  local match_counter = 0
  search.search_async(h.fixtures, "foo", {}, function(match)
    eq("foo", match.submatches[1].match.text)
    match_counter = match_counter + 1
  end, function(exit_code)
    eq(0, exit_code)
    eq(8, match_counter)
  end)
end
```

for now if I use `make test` (setup properly), this test is not included in the result. Same as I do `:lua MiniTest.run_file()`. But if the test has an error, the latter would print the proper formatted error message in the current neovim session.


I know in busted tests there's a way to mark a test as async: https://lunarmodules.github.io/busted/#async-tests

I would like to see similar capability.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

The posted code snippet has several issues that go against the 'mini.test' design:
- Every test case function is only executed as is with possible arguments from `parametrize`. There is no other automated tweaking of it per se and it is assumed to be a test writer responsibility to ensure that it throws errors when the condition is not right. This explains why there is no error reported when there are ones.
- It is highly suggested for test cases to use child Neovim process to actually test the behavior. I.e. executing tested feature and gathering information about the process state should be done inside child process. This makes each test case separate with clean environment. See [using child process section](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/TESTING.md#using-child-process). This explains why errors are reported in the current process outside of 'mini.test' results.

The suggested solution here is to:
- Create and properly reset child process in each test case. See link above. Make sure that tested plugin is set up inside child process.
- Execute `search.search_async` inside child process. Like with `child.lua([[ ... ]])`.
- Wait for child process to execute async callback. Either:
    - Use `vim.wait` inside child process to make it synchronous and later return tested state.
    - Sleep outside of child process and later get its state. I usually prefer using this approach.

So, I'd have this test written something like this:

```lua
local child = MiniTest.new_child_neovim()
local eq = MiniTest.expect.equality
local small_time = 10

local sleep = function(duration)
  vim.loop.sleep(math.max(duration, 1))
  child.poke_eventloop()
end

T["search_async"] = new_set()

T['search_async']['should find files with search term in content'] = function()
  child.lua([[
    local match_counter = 0
    _G.log = {}

    search.search_async(h.fixtures, 'foo', {}, function(match)
      table.insert(_G.log, { match_text = match.submatches[1].match.text })
      match_counter = match_counter + 1
    end, function(exit_code)
      table.insert(_G.log, { exit_code = exit_code, match_counter = match_counter })
    end)
  ]])

  sleep(small_time)

  local ref_log = { { match_text = 'foo' }, { exit_code = 0, match_counter = 8 } }
  eq(child.lua_get('_G.log'), ref_log)
end
```

---

Closing as both "not planned" and "already possible".
